issues.legal_issue: A decree may be corrected after judgment to complete an accidentally incomplete property description when the property is sufficiently identifiable from the record and the correction does not substitute different property or decide a disputed question.
material_facts: A suit sought declaration of title and possession, and the decree repeated a property schedule that omitted particulars including the area, plot numbers and khatian numbers.
The body of the plaint described the land, and the conveyance documents and evidence referred to the relevant plots and land.
The correction application sought to insert missing particulars; the objecting defendant argued that the changed locality number would substitute a different property.
The defendant had testified in the suit, and the Court found that the pleadings sufficiently described the land and that the defendant had not been misled.
The amendment was allowed after the decree, and the order allowing it was challenged in an appeal.
issues.conclusion: The correction was permissible and the appeal against the order allowing it was dismissed; the amendment completed the description rather than substituting another property or reopening the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure permit a court to correct an accidental slip or omission in a judgment or decree so that the record expresses the court’s meaning and intention. The power may extend to an error originating in a party’s description and carried into the decree, but only where the intended correction is clear and does not require resolution of disputed questions or review of the merits. The Court relied on Samarendra Nath Sinha v. Krishna Kumar Nag, Bela Debi v. Bon Behary Roy, Lakshmi Ram Bhuyan v. Hari Prasad Bhuyan, Pratibha Singh v. Shanti Devi Prasad, and State of Punjab v. Darshan Singh, and also referred to Dwaraka Das v. State of Madhya Pradesh and Jayalakshmi Coelho v. Oswald Joseph Coelho as confirming that the correction power cannot be used to alter the substance of a final decision.

rule.if: appeal_from_order_allowing_post_decree_correction and schedule_omissions_were_inadvertent and body_of_pleading_identified_property and correction_completed_description and correction_did_not_substitute_property and correction_required_no_resolution_of_disputed_questions

predicates.appeal_from_order_allowing_post_decree_c: A party appealed from an order allowing correction of a decree after it had been entered.
predicates.schedule_omissions_were_inadvertent: The property schedule omitted identifying particulars because of an asserted inadvertence in drafting.
predicates.body_of_pleading_identified_property: The body of the pleading contained information identifying the property despite omissions in its schedule.
predicates.correction_completed_description: The proposed correction added particulars to complete the description already appearing in the record.
predicates.correction_did_not_substitute_property: The proposed correction described the same property rather than replacing it with different property.
predicates.correction_required_no_resolution_of_dis: The court could determine the intended correction from the record without deciding a disputed issue about what property the parties intended to deal with.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a post-decree correction, an inadvertent omission may be corrected if the record identifies the property, the correction completes rather than replaces its description, and no disputed question must be resolved.

issues.legal_issue: A person who was not a party to a suit is not bound by its decree and may pursue remedies available by law if the decree affects that person’s claimed interest or possession.
material_facts: An applicant seeking impleadment asserted an interest in and possession of land affected by the decree.
The applicant had not been a party to the suit in which the decree was made.
The application for impleadment was considered in the appeal concerning correction of the decree.
issues.conclusion: The applicant was not bound by the decree and could pursue remedies available in law, including an application under Order 21 Rules 97 and 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure if an occasion arose; the application for impleadment was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A decree does not bind a person who was not a party to the suit. Such a person may seek remedies available under law, including the procedures in Order 21 Rules 97 and 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure where applicable. The Court left any such claim to be determined according to law and did not decide the applicant’s claimed rights.

predicates.application_to_join_decree_appeal: A person applied to be joined in an appeal concerning a decree made in an earlier suit.
predicates.claimant_was_not_party_to_suit: The person seeking to be joined had not been a party to the suit in which the decree was made.
predicates.claimant_asserted_independent_interest_o: The person seeking to be joined asserted an interest in or possession of property affected by the decree.

issues.definition: When a person seeking to join an appeal was not a party to the suit but asserts an independent interest or possession, that person is not bound by the decree and may pursue available remedies.

issues.legal_issue: The executing court must consider whether a decree presents difficulty in execution when the property description has required correction.
material_facts: The decree concerned identified land but its schedule had omitted particulars that were later inserted by correction.
The appeal against the order allowing correction was dismissed, while the Court left practical execution of the decree for consideration by the executing court.
issues.conclusion: The executing court was to consider at the time of execution whether any difficulty in executing the decree existed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed the executing court to assess any practical difficulty in executing the decree; it cited no separate statutory provision or earlier case for this direction.

predicates.decree_requires_execution: A decree remains to be carried out through execution proceedings.
predicates.property_description_was_corrected: The description of property in the decree has been corrected after the decree was made.

issues.definition: When a decree remains to be executed and its property description has been corrected, the executing court must assess whether execution presents difficulty.
